### Recommendation
Prioritise Area A for the next campaign.
Evidence level: **strong** (strong = 95% interval of the difference excludes zero and >= 10 campaign rows; negative ROI = do not expand; otherwise a limited controlled test).

### Evidence
| area | rows | spend | revenue | ROI | CAC | conversion rate (95% CI) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Area A | 14 | 81,053.04 | 169,616.36 | 109.3% | 80.01 | 6.7% (6.3% to 7.1%) |
| Area B | 14 | 77,170.89 | 102,864.30 | 33.3% | 114.84 | 4.7% (4.4% to 5.0%) |
| Area C | 14 | 87,464.47 | 94,326.82 | 7.8% | 131.13 | 4.0% (3.7% to 4.3%) |
| Area D | 14 | 73,380.50 | 37,091.71 | -49.5% | 179.41 | 3.0% (2.7% to 3.3%) |
| Area E | 2 | 11,936.14 | 18,555.21 | 55.5% | 98.65 | 5.6% (4.7% to 6.7%) |

- Per-campaign ROI in Area A averaged 107.5% vs -0.1% elsewhere: difference 107.6% (95% CI 79.8% to 135.4%, Welch's t-test p < 0.001, Hedges' g = 2.46).
- Conversion rate in Area A 6.7% vs 4.0% elsewhere: difference 2.7% (95% CI 2.2% to 3.1%, chi-square test of independence p < 0.001; expected counts adequate for chi-square).
- Over time in Area A: ROI 100.6% in 2025-01-01 to 2025-07-01, then 116.7% in 2025-08-01 to 2026-02-01.

### Methodology
- Grouped 58 campaign rows by 'area'; columns used: spend = 'ad_spend', revenue = 'revenue', leads = 'leads', conversions = 'conversions', date = 'month' (chosen by name: column name 'ad_spend' matches 'ad_?spend'; column name 'revenue' matches 'revenue'; column name 'leads' matches 'leads?'; column name 'conversions' matches 'conversions?'; column name 'area' matches 'area'; 'month' is the only date column).
- ROI = (revenue - spend) / spend; CAC = spend / conversions; conversion rate = conversions / leads with a Wilson 95% interval.
- Ranked groups by ROI ((revenue - spend) / spend); compared the focus group with all others combined (Welch's t-test on per-campaign ROI; chi-square or Fisher's exact test on conversion counts).
- No Random Forest or other predictive model was used: this is an analysis of historical results.

### Limitations
- Observational data: it shows results where money was spent, not what spending caused (areas that received more budget may differ in other ways).
- Not compared (fewer than 3 rows): Area E.
- Past returns may not hold at a higher budget (diminishing returns are not visible in this data).

### Next action
Run a controlled experiment: raise spend in part of the area (or for a period) and keep a comparable holdout, then compare conversions and ROI between them.
